must_remember: Proper time ($t_0$) is measured by a clock at rest relative to the events, representing the shortest time interval between two events in inertial frames.
The Lorentz factor $\gamma = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \frac{v^2}{c^2}}}$ governs the magnitude of relativistic time dilation.
Time dilation is completely reciprocal between two inertially moving observers, meaning each sees the other's clock running slow.
Atmospheric muon decay serves as direct experimental verification of time dilation, allowing high-speed cosmic ray muons to reach sea level.
The Twin Paradox is resolved because the traveling twin undergoes acceleration and changes inertial frames, breaking the initial symmetry.

glossary.meaning: The time interval measured by a clock that is at rest relative to the events being observed, occurring at the same spatial point in that frame.
The time interval measured by an observer in relative motion with respect to the clock, always greater than the proper time interval.
The dimensionless scaling factor $\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}}$ by which time, length, and relativistic mass change.
A thought experiment in special relativity involving identical twins, one of whom makes a journey into space in a high-speed rocket and returns to find the stay-at-home twin has aged more.
